small_guidance:
- The epilogue kernel is already memory-bound and tiny relative to the ConvTranspose3d (which dominates the 10.1 ms runtime); further tuning of BLOCK_SIZE/num_warps will not close the gap. If kept, try BLOCK_SIZE=16384 with num_warps=8, num_stages=3, and flatten the grid to 1D over N*C*S to reduce launch overhead.
- Fold the bias add into the conv epilogue by writing directly to a channels-last contiguous buffer so the bias broadcast is a single contiguous load per channel.
- Replace `bias` indexing via `nc % C` with a precomputed channel-major grid (program_id(0)=channel, program_id(1)=N*spatial tile) to avoid the modulo.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.ConvTranspose3d` with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per (N, IC tile, input-spatial tile) computing the outer product `input[n,ic,d,h,w] * weight[ic,oc,kd,kh,kw]` and atomically scattering into the output grid with stride=2, padding=1, output_padding=1 index math. This is the heavy op (~9.5 ms of the 10.1 ms total) and has all the headroom.
- Alternatively, implement it as a gather-style GEMM: one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile) where each output voxel iterates over the (kd,kh,kw,ic) positions whose stride-2 placement lands on it — typically only 1 valid (kd,kh,kw) combination per output position, making it cheap. Fuse bias + `(2x+b)*x + x` epilogue directly into the store.
- Use channels-last (NDHWC) layout for both input and output so the IC/OC contraction axis is contiguous and loads coalesce; precompute weight in (kd,kh,kw,ic,oc) layout at init time.
